title: Singular partitive of -nen words
summary: Form the singular partitive in this bounded word family.
objectives: Form the singular partitive in this bounded word family.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: A case is a word form used for a grammatical job. The dictionary form is the form used to look up a word. The partitive has several uses; it does not always mean “some”. Here you practise forming the word, so no sentence construction is required.
Replace final -nen with -sta/-stä in this family. The result contains st. The same pattern can form a noun or an adjective; adjective agreement is taught separately.
keyPoints: Learn each word with its pattern; a similar final letter does not guarantee the same stem.

steps: Remove -nen from nainen and add sta: naista.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “woman”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Remove -nen from suomalainen and add sta: suomalaista.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “Finnish”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Remove -nen from ihminen and add stä: ihmistä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “person”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Remove -nen from hevonen and add sta: hevosta.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “horse”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Remove -nen from lautanen and add sta: lautasta.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “plate”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Remove -nen from punainen and add sta: punaista.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “red”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Remove -nen from sininen and add stä: sinistä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “blue”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Remove -nen from iloinen and add sta: iloista.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “happy”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.

commonMistakes: Replace -nen; do not attach an ending after the whole -nen word.
Keep the st sequence in the resulting form.
The word family is shared by nouns and adjectives.
